parsed.explanation: The 1861 same-sex statute is secondary: no prosecution against trans visitors is documented. The core evidence is police harassment, detention, beatings, and public humiliation of people perceived as LGBT, specifically men dressed as women, with no formal charge and no statutory recourse. That is state-directed targeting on gender expression, not mere social friction. A 2004 lethal anti-LGBT case with impunity reinforces hostility but is too old and singular to establish a current killing rate. Sources are dated and thin; silence in later reports about prosecutions is not evidence of safety or reform. There is no documented subnational variation or working remedy. Severity if outed is moderate-to-high; probability is elevated by visible presentation and police spot-checking. This places the jurisdiction at the high-risk side of the elevated/high boundary, around 0.31.
